name: Arch
description: Local stdio server from tnvolman/arch-cursor-plugin. To get Guard's review defaults, set the MCP command to the script path so the basename is index.mjs, not node plus args. At eaf99bbc server/index.mjs is mode 100644, not executable. arch_review POSTs {text, max_tokens?, payment_method_id?, idempotency_key?} to https://arch.tnvolman.com/v1/review and sends ARCH_API_KEY as X-API-Key. kjv_lookup sends nothing. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: To get Guard's review defaults, set the MCP command to the script path itself so the basename is index.mjs. Guard matches any stdio command named index.mjs. node plus args is not matched.
Published mcp.json uses node and ./server/index.mjs. At eaf99bbc that file is mode 100644, not executable, despite its node shebang. There is no PRIVACY.md in the plugin repo.

arch_review only POSTs JSON {text, max_tokens?, payment_method_id?, idempotency_key?} to https://arch.tnvolman.com/v1/review. Code sets Content-Type, Accept, X-API-Key (the ARCH_API_KEY value), and Idempotency-Key when idempotency_key is non-empty.

If ARCH_API_KEY is missing or empty, or text is empty or over 50000 characters, arch_review sends nothing. kjv_lookup only reads bundled server/data/kjv.json and sends no reference, verse text, or API key.

The plugin does not write the review text or the key. https://arch.tnvolman.com/privacy (updated 19 October 2026) says Arch sends the text to Anthropic, holds it in memory for the request, then discards it, and does not store it in its database.

That policy says call count and last-used time on the key, and a charge ledger of payment-intent id, amount, currency, status, and character count (not the text), stay until deleted on request. Railway logs record character count and key prefix.

Operational logs record character count, not the text. Anthropic retention, Railway log duration, and whether logs keep the full X-API-Key are unverified. The policy says review text is not used to train models.

The privacy page says Cloudflare and Railway see IP, user agent, and timestamps. How long they keep that metadata is unverified. The plugin calls only POST /v1/review. Extra headers from Node fetch are unverified.
